metadata.task: SQLite Database Schema Design for Token-Efficient I/O
inputs_consumed: KB-0001.md (sample KB entry with YAML frontmatter)
design_principles: Source files remain canonical truth; DB is a generated query layer
Single SQLite DB replaces all 9+ index.json files
Projection queries return only requested fields
Auto-increment IDs for new entry creation
Views replicate current index formats for backward compatibility
CHECK constraints enforce naming conventions at DB level
WAL mode for concurrent multi-agent read access

tables.name: entries
tables.description: Unified table for all resource types: KB entries, SOPs, sources, scripts, team logs, API tools

columns.name: confidence
columns.constraints: DEFAULT NULL CHECK(confidence IS NULL OR confidence IN ('low','medium','high','very-high'))

tables.notes: The 'id' column stores the human-readable ID (e.g., 'KB-0001'). 'numeric_id' stores the integer portion for auto-increment. 'extra_json' stores type-specific fields as JSON (e.g., for TOOL: modules, entry_point, requires; for SRC: url, data_types, access_type; for SCR: language, dependencies, filename).

tables.name: tags
tables.description: Many-to-many tag associations. Replaces the tag_index sections in all index.json files.

columns.name: entry_id
columns.constraints: NOT NULL REFERENCES entries(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

tables.notes: Enables queries like: SELECT entry_id FROM tags WHERE tag = 'database'. The unique composite index prevents duplicate tag assignments.

tables.name: relationships
tables.description: Graph edges between entries. Captures builds_on chains, supersedes links, and cross-references.

columns.name: source_id
columns.constraints: NOT NULL REFERENCES entries(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

columns.name: target_id
columns.constraints: NOT NULL REFERENCES entries(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

tables.notes: Enables recursive CTE queries for ancestry chains. Example: WITH RECURSIVE chain AS (SELECT target_id FROM relationships WHERE source_id = 'KB-0031' AND rel_type = 'builds_on' UNION ALL SELECT r.target_id FROM relationships r JOIN chain c ON r.source_id = c.target_id WHERE r.rel_type = 'builds_on') SELECT * FROM chain;

tables.name: id_sequences
tables.description: Tracks the next available numeric ID for each resource type. Replaces manual max-ID scanning of index.json.
tables.notes: Atomic ID assignment: UPDATE id_sequences SET next_id = next_id + 1 WHERE resource_type = 'KB' RETURNING next_id - 1. Eliminates race conditions in multi-agent entry creation.

tables.name: changes
tables.description: Incremental change log for session-aware differential reads. Records what changed and when.
tables.notes: Agents can query: SELECT * FROM changes WHERE timestamp > '2026-03-11T10:00:00' to see what changed since their last session. Populated by triggers on entries table.

fts5.create_sql: CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE IF NOT EXISTS entries_fts USING fts5(title, summary, description, content=entries, content_rowid=rowid, tokenize='unicode61 remove_diacritics 2');

sync_triggers.after_insert: CREATE TRIGGER entries_fts_ai AFTER INSERT ON entries BEGIN INSERT INTO entries_fts(rowid, title, summary, description) VALUES (new.rowid, new.title, new.summary, new.description); END;
sync_triggers.after_update: CREATE TRIGGER entries_fts_au AFTER UPDATE ON entries BEGIN INSERT INTO entries_fts(entries_fts, rowid, title, summary, description) VALUES ('delete', old.rowid, old.title, old.summary, old.description); INSERT INTO entries_fts(rowid, title, summary, description) VALUES (new.rowid, new.title, new.summary, new.description); END;
sync_triggers.after_delete: CREATE TRIGGER entries_fts_ad AFTER DELETE ON entries BEGIN INSERT INTO entries_fts(entries_fts, rowid, title, summary, description) VALUES ('delete', old.rowid, old.title, old.summary, old.description); END;

query_examples.description: Search for entries about databases, ranked by relevance
query_examples.sql: SELECT e.id, e.title, e.resource_type, rank FROM entries_fts f JOIN entries e ON f.rowid = e.rowid WHERE entries_fts MATCH 'database' ORDER BY rank LIMIT 10;

query_examples.description: Phrase search with column weighting (title 10x, summary 5x, description 1x)
query_examples.sql: SELECT e.id, e.title, bm25(entries_fts, 10.0, 5.0, 1.0) AS score FROM entries_fts f JOIN entries e ON f.rowid = e.rowid WHERE entries_fts MATCH 'multi-agent coordination' ORDER BY score LIMIT 5;
SELECT e.id, e.title FROM entries_fts f JOIN entries e ON f.rowid = e.rowid WHERE entries_fts MATCH 'title:optimization' ORDER BY rank;

fts5.notes: External-content mode avoids data duplication — the FTS index references the entries table. The unicode61 tokenizer handles international characters and strips diacritics for robust matching. BM25 ranking is built-in. Highlight() and snippet() functions available for context-aware result presentation.

views.name: v_kb_index
views.purpose: Replicates knowledge-base/index.json structure. Returns all KB entries with their tags and builds_on relationships.
views.sql: CREATE VIEW v_kb_index AS SELECT e.id, e.title, e.created_date AS date, e.team, e.category, e.status, e.confidence, (SELECT json_group_array(t.tag) FROM tags t WHERE t.entry_id = e.id) AS tags, (SELECT json_group_array(r.target_id) FROM relationships r WHERE r.source_id = e.id AND r.rel_type = 'builds_on') AS builds_on FROM entries e WHERE e.resource_type = 'KB' ORDER BY e.numeric_id;

views.name: v_sop_index
views.sql: CREATE VIEW v_sop_index AS SELECT e.id, e.title, e.file_path AS filename, e.version, e.status, e.description, (SELECT json_group_array(r.target_id) FROM relationships r WHERE r.source_id = e.id AND r.rel_type = 'supersedes') AS supersedes FROM entries e WHERE e.resource_type = 'SOP' ORDER BY e.numeric_id;

views.name: v_scripts_index
views.sql: CREATE VIEW v_scripts_index AS SELECT e.id, e.title AS name, json_extract(e.extra_json, '$.filename') AS filename, json_extract(e.extra_json, '$.language') AS language, e.category, e.description, e.created_date AS added, e.team AS added_by_team, (SELECT json_group_array(t.tag) FROM tags t WHERE t.entry_id = e.id) AS tags FROM entries e WHERE e.resource_type = 'SCR' ORDER BY e.numeric_id;

views.name: v_sources_index
views.sql: CREATE VIEW v_sources_index AS SELECT e.id, e.title AS name, json_extract(e.extra_json, '$.url') AS url, json_extract(e.extra_json, '$.data_types') AS data_types, json_extract(e.extra_json, '$.access_type') AS access_type, (SELECT json_group_array(t.tag) FROM tags t WHERE t.entry_id = e.id) AS tags FROM entries e WHERE e.resource_type = 'SRC' ORDER BY e.numeric_id;

views.name: v_tools_index
views.sql: CREATE VIEW v_tools_index AS SELECT e.id, e.title AS name, e.description, json_extract(e.extra_json, '$.path') AS path, e.category, json_extract(e.extra_json, '$.auth_type') AS auth_type, e.created_date AS date_added, e.team, json_extract(e.extra_json, '$.modules') AS modules, json_extract(e.extra_json, '$.entry_point') AS entry_point, json_extract(e.extra_json, '$.requires') AS requires, (SELECT json_group_array(t.tag) FROM tags t WHERE t.entry_id = e.id) AS tags FROM entries e WHERE e.resource_type = 'TOOL' ORDER BY e.numeric_id;

views.name: v_teams_index
views.sql: CREATE VIEW v_teams_index AS SELECT e.id AS team_id, json_extract(e.extra_json, '$.filename') AS filename, e.created_date AS date, e.description AS objective, (SELECT json_group_array(r.target_id) FROM relationships r WHERE r.source_id = e.id AND r.rel_type = 'builds_on') AS builds_on_knowledge, json_extract(e.extra_json, '$.members') AS members FROM entries e WHERE e.resource_type = 'TEAM' ORDER BY e.numeric_id;

views.name: v_compact
views.purpose: Level 1 compact view: minimal fields for orientation. ~15 tokens per entry, ~500 tokens for all 31 KB entries.
views.sql: CREATE VIEW v_compact AS SELECT e.id, e.title, e.resource_type, e.category, e.created_date AS date FROM entries e ORDER BY e.resource_type, e.numeric_id;

views.name: v_summary
views.purpose: Level 0 summary view: aggregate counts by type for instant orientation. ~50 tokens total.
views.sql: CREATE VIEW v_summary AS SELECT resource_type, COUNT(*) AS entry_count, MAX(updated_date) AS last_updated, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT category) AS categories FROM entries GROUP BY resource_type ORDER BY resource_type;

views.name: v_recent
views.purpose: Last 10 entries across all types, with summaries. For quick session onboarding.
views.sql: CREATE VIEW v_recent AS SELECT e.id, e.title, e.resource_type, e.summary, e.created_date AS date FROM entries e ORDER BY e.created_date DESC, e.numeric_id DESC LIMIT 10;

views.name: v_tag_cloud
views.purpose: Tag frequency counts for topic overview. ~100 tokens total.
views.sql: CREATE VIEW v_tag_cloud AS SELECT tag, COUNT(*) AS usage_count FROM tags GROUP BY tag ORDER BY usage_count DESC;

views.name: v_category_counts
views.purpose: Entry counts per category per resource type. ~30 tokens.
views.sql: CREATE VIEW v_category_counts AS SELECT resource_type, category, COUNT(*) AS count FROM entries GROUP BY resource_type, category ORDER BY resource_type, count DESC;

views.name: v_ancestry
views.purpose: Flattened builds_on graph showing direct parent-child links for quick relationship discovery.
views.sql: CREATE VIEW v_ancestry AS SELECT r.source_id AS child_id, e1.title AS child_title, r.target_id AS parent_id, e2.title AS parent_title FROM relationships r JOIN entries e1 ON r.source_id = e1.id JOIN entries e2 ON r.target_id = e2.id WHERE r.rel_type = 'builds_on' ORDER BY r.source_id;

triggers.name: trg_entries_token_estimate_insert
triggers.sql: -- token_estimate is a GENERATED column: see entries table definition. No trigger needed.
triggers.purpose: Token estimate is computed as a GENERATED ALWAYS AS (char_count / 4) STORED column on the entries table. This avoids trigger cascade issues entirely.

triggers.name: trg_entries_updated_date
triggers.sql: -- updated_date is set by the application (import script / MCP server) on each write to avoid trigger cascades.
triggers.purpose: updated_date is managed by the application layer. The import script sets it from file modification time; the MCP server sets it to date('now') on writes.

triggers.name: trg_changes_insert
triggers.sql: CREATE TRIGGER trg_changes_insert AFTER INSERT ON entries BEGIN INSERT INTO changes(entry_id, change_type, summary) VALUES (new.id, 'insert', 'New ' || new.resource_type || ': ' || new.title); END;
triggers.purpose: Log entry creation to changes table

triggers.name: trg_changes_update
triggers.sql: CREATE TRIGGER trg_changes_update AFTER UPDATE ON entries BEGIN INSERT INTO changes(entry_id, change_type, summary) VALUES (new.id, 'update', 'Updated ' || new.resource_type || ': ' || new.title); END;
triggers.purpose: Log entry updates to changes table

triggers.name: trg_changes_delete
triggers.sql: CREATE TRIGGER trg_changes_delete AFTER DELETE ON entries BEGIN INSERT INTO changes(entry_id, change_type, summary) VALUES (old.id, 'delete', 'Deleted ' || old.resource_type || ': ' || old.title); END;
triggers.purpose: Log entry deletions to changes table

check_constraints.constraint: Enforced via application-level validation at insert time: KB-XXXX, SOP-XXX, SRC-XXXX, SCR-XXXX, TEAM-XXXX, TOOL-XXXX
check_constraints.rationale: SQLite CHECK constraints do not support REGEXP natively. Naming validation is enforced by the import script and MCP server, not at the SQL level. The id_sequences table ensures numeric portions are sequential.
Restricts resource types to the 6 known types. Adding a new type requires a schema migration.
Enforces the 200-character max for pre-computed summaries. Keeps Level 1 queries token-efficient.

check_constraints.constraint: CHECK(confidence IS NULL OR confidence IN ('low','medium','high','very-high'))
check_constraints.rationale: Controlled vocabulary for confidence levels. NULL allowed for resource types that don't use confidence.
Controlled vocabulary for relationship types. Covers all current patterns: builds_on (KB entries), supersedes (SOP versions), references (cross-type links), related (inferred connections).

migration_sql:
-- ============================================
-- Registry Database Schema v1.0
-- Generated by B2-Gamma for token-efficient I/O
-- Date: 2026-03-11
-- ============================================

PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL;
PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;
PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000;

-- ============================================
-- Core Tables
-- ============================================

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS entries (
    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    numeric_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    resource_type TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(resource_type IN ('KB','SOP','SRC','SCR','TEAM','TOOL')),
    title TEXT NOT NULL,
    summary TEXT CHECK(length(summary) <= 200),
    category TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
    status TEXT DEFAULT 'active',
    confidence TEXT DEFAULT NULL CHECK(confidence IS NULL OR confidence IN ('low','medium','high','very-high')),
    file_path TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    content_hash TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
    created_date TEXT DEFAULT (date('now')),
    updated_date TEXT DEFAULT (date('now')),
    team TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
    char_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    token_estimate INTEGER GENERATED ALWAYS AS (char_count / 4) STORED,
    version TEXT DEFAULT '1.0',
    description TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
    extra_json TEXT DEFAULT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tags (
    entry_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES entries(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    tag TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(length(tag) > 0),
    UNIQUE(entry_id, tag)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS relationships (
    source_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES entries(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    target_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES entries(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    rel_type TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(rel_type IN ('builds_on','supersedes','references','related')),
    metadata TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
    UNIQUE(source_id, target_id, rel_type)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS id_sequences (
    resource_type TEXT PRIMARY KEY CHECK(resource_type IN ('KB','SOP','SRC','SCR','TEAM','TOOL')),
    next_id INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS changes (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    timestamp TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
    entry_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    change_type TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(change_type IN ('insert','update','delete')),
    changed_fields TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
    summary TEXT DEFAULT NULL
);

-- ============================================
-- Indexes
-- ============================================

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_entries_resource_type ON entries(resource_type);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_entries_category ON entries(category);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_entries_status ON entries(status);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_entries_team ON entries(team);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_entries_created_date ON entries(created_date);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_entries_type_category ON entries(resource_type, category);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_entries_type_date ON entries(resource_type, created_date DESC);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_entries_type_numeric ON entries(resource_type, numeric_id);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_tags_entry_id ON tags(entry_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_tags_tag ON tags(tag);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_rel_source ON relationships(source_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_rel_target ON relationships(target_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_rel_type ON relationships(rel_type);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_changes_timestamp ON changes(timestamp);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_changes_entry_id ON changes(entry_id);

-- ============================================
-- FTS5 Full-Text Search
-- ============================================

CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE IF NOT EXISTS entries_fts USING fts5(
    title,
    summary,
    description,
    content=entries,
    content_rowid=rowid,
    tokenize='unicode61 remove_diacritics 2'
);

-- FTS5 sync triggers (external-content mode)
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS entries_fts_ai AFTER INSERT ON entries BEGIN
    INSERT INTO entries_fts(rowid, title, summary, description)
    VALUES (new.rowid, new.title, new.summary, new.description);
END;

CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS entries_fts_au AFTER UPDATE ON entries BEGIN
    INSERT INTO entries_fts(entries_fts, rowid, title, summary, description)
    VALUES ('delete', old.rowid, old.title, old.summary, old.description);
    INSERT INTO entries_fts(rowid, title, summary, description)
    VALUES (new.rowid, new.title, new.summary, new.description);
END;

CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS entries_fts_ad AFTER DELETE ON entries BEGIN
    INSERT INTO entries_fts(entries_fts, rowid, title, summary, description)
    VALUES ('delete', old.rowid, old.title, old.summary, old.description);
END;

-- ============================================
-- Application Triggers
-- ============================================

-- token_estimate is a GENERATED ALWAYS AS (char_count / 4) STORED column.
-- No trigger needed for token estimation.

-- updated_date is managed by the application layer to avoid trigger cascades.
-- The import script and MCP server set updated_date explicitly on each write.

CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS trg_changes_insert AFTER INSERT ON entries
BEGIN
    INSERT INTO changes(entry_id, change_type, summary)
    VALUES (new.id, 'insert', 'New ' || new.resource_type || ': ' || new.title);
END;

CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS trg_changes_update AFTER UPDATE ON entries
BEGIN
    INSERT INTO changes(entry_id, change_type, summary)
    VALUES (new.id, 'update', 'Updated ' || new.resource_type || ': ' || new.title);
END;

CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS trg_changes_delete AFTER DELETE ON entries
BEGIN
    INSERT INTO changes(entry_id, change_type, summary)
    VALUES (old.id, 'delete', 'Deleted ' || old.resource_type || ': ' || old.title);
END;

-- ============================================
-- Views
-- ============================================

-- Level 0: Aggregate summary (~50 tokens)
CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS v_summary AS
SELECT resource_type,
       COUNT(*) AS entry_count,
       MAX(updated_date) AS last_updated,
       GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT category) AS categories
FROM entries
GROUP BY resource_type
ORDER BY resource_type;

-- Level 1: Compact index (~15 tokens per entry)
CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS v_compact AS
SELECT e.id, e.title, e.resource_type, e.category, e.created_date AS date
FROM entries e
ORDER BY e.resource_type, e.numeric_id;

-- Recent entries for session onboarding
CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS v_recent AS
SELECT e.id, e.title, e.resource_type, e.summary, e.created_date AS date
FROM entries e
ORDER BY e.created_date DESC, e.numeric_id DESC
LIMIT 10;

-- Tag frequency cloud
CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS v_tag_cloud AS
SELECT tag, COUNT(*) AS usage_count
FROM tags
GROUP BY tag
ORDER BY usage_count DESC;

-- Category counts by resource type
CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS v_category_counts AS
SELECT resource_type, category, COUNT(*) AS count
FROM entries
GROUP BY resource_type, category
ORDER BY resource_type, count DESC;

-- Knowledge Base index (replicates knowledge-base/index.json)
CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS v_kb_index AS
SELECT e.id, e.title, e.created_date AS date, e.team, e.category, e.status, e.confidence,
       (SELECT json_group_array(t.tag) FROM tags t WHERE t.entry_id = e.id) AS tags,
       (SELECT json_group_array(r.target_id) FROM relationships r WHERE r.source_id = e.id AND r.rel_type = 'builds_on') AS builds_on
FROM entries e
WHERE e.resource_type = 'KB'
ORDER BY e.numeric_id;

-- SOP index (replicates sops/index.json)
CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS v_sop_index AS
SELECT e.id, e.title, e.file_path AS filename, e.version, e.status, e.description,
       (SELECT json_group_array(r.target_id) FROM relationships r WHERE r.source_id = e.id AND r.rel_type = 'supersedes') AS supersedes
FROM entries e
WHERE e.resource_type = 'SOP'
ORDER BY e.numeric_id;

-- Scripts index (replicates scripts/index.json)
CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS v_scripts_index AS
SELECT e.id, e.title AS name,
       json_extract(e.extra_json, '$.filename') AS filename,
       json_extract(e.extra_json, '$.language') AS language,
       e.category, e.description,
       e.created_date AS added, e.team AS added_by_team,
       (SELECT json_group_array(t.tag) FROM tags t WHERE t.entry_id = e.id) AS tags
FROM entries e
WHERE e.resource_type = 'SCR'
ORDER BY e.numeric_id;

-- Sources index (replicates sources/index.json)
CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS v_sources_index AS
SELECT e.id, e.title AS name,
       json_extract(e.extra_json, '$.url') AS url,
       json_extract(e.extra_json, '$.data_types') AS data_types,
       json_extract(e.extra_json, '$.access_type') AS access_type,
       (SELECT json_group_array(t.tag) FROM tags t WHERE t.entry_id = e.id) AS tags
FROM entries e
WHERE e.resource_type = 'SRC'
ORDER BY e.numeric_id;

-- Tools index (replicates api-tools/index.json)
CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS v_tools_index AS
SELECT e.id, e.title AS name, e.description,
       json_extract(e.extra_json, '$.path') AS path,
       e.category,
       json_extract(e.extra_json, '$.auth_type') AS auth_type,
       e.created_date AS date_added, e.team,
       json_extract(e.extra_json, '$.modules') AS modules,
       json_extract(e.extra_json, '$.entry_point') AS entry_point,
       json_extract(e.extra_json, '$.requires') AS requires,
       (SELECT json_group_array(t.tag) FROM tags t WHERE t.entry_id = e.id) AS tags
FROM entries e
WHERE e.resource_type = 'TOOL'
ORDER BY e.numeric_id;

-- Teams index (replicates teams/sessions/index.json)
CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS v_teams_index AS
SELECT e.id AS team_id,
       json_extract(e.extra_json, '$.filename') AS filename,
       e.created_date AS date,
       e.description AS objective,
       (SELECT json_group_array(r.target_id) FROM relationships r WHERE r.source_id = e.id AND r.rel_type = 'builds_on') AS builds_on_knowledge,
       json_extract(e.extra_json, '$.members') AS members
FROM entries e
WHERE e.resource_type = 'TEAM'
ORDER BY e.numeric_id;

-- Ancestry graph view
CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS v_ancestry AS
SELECT r.source_id AS child_id, e1.title AS child_title,
       r.target_id AS parent_id, e2.title AS parent_title
FROM relationships r
JOIN entries e1 ON r.source_id = e1.id
JOIN entries e2 ON r.target_id = e2.id
WHERE r.rel_type = 'builds_on'
ORDER BY r.source_id;

-- ============================================
-- Seed ID Sequences
-- ============================================

INSERT OR IGNORE INTO id_sequences(resource_type, next_id) VALUES ('KB', 32);
INSERT OR IGNORE INTO id_sequences(resource_type, next_id) VALUES ('SOP', 26);
INSERT OR IGNORE INTO id_sequences(resource_type, next_id) VALUES ('SRC', 42);
INSERT OR IGNORE INTO id_sequences(resource_type, next_id) VALUES ('SCR', 30);
INSERT OR IGNORE INTO id_sequences(resource_type, next_id) VALUES ('TEAM', 30);
INSERT OR IGNORE INTO id_sequences(resource_type, next_id) VALUES ('TOOL', 4);
import_pseudocode:
# Import Process: Populate registry.db from existing source files
# Run once at setup, then on-demand via pre-commit hook or generate_index.py

import sqlite3, hashlib, json, yaml, os, glob

# Step 1: Create database and apply schema
db = sqlite3.connect('storage/registry.db')
db.executescript(MIGRATION_SQL)  # The migration_sql string above

# Step 2: Import KB entries (knowledge-base/entries/KB-*.md)
for filepath in sorted(glob.glob('knowledge-base/entries/KB-*.md')):
    content = read_file(filepath)
    frontmatter = parse_yaml_frontmatter(content)  # Extract YAML between --- delimiters
    body = extract_body(content)  # Everything after second ---
    
    entry_id = frontmatter['id']  # e.g., 'KB-0001'
    numeric_id = int(entry_id.split('-')[1])  # e.g., 1
    char_count = len(content)
    content_hash = hashlib.sha256(content.encode()).hexdigest()
    summary = generate_summary(body, max_chars=200)  # First sentence or ## Result first line
    
    db.execute('''INSERT INTO entries (id, numeric_id, resource_type, title, summary, category,
        status, confidence, file_path, content_hash, created_date, team, char_count, description)
        VALUES (?, ?, 'KB', ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)''',
        (entry_id, numeric_id, frontmatter['title'], summary,
         frontmatter.get('category'), frontmatter.get('status', 'active'),
         frontmatter.get('confidence'), filepath, content_hash,
         frontmatter.get('date'), frontmatter.get('team'), char_count,
         extract_first_paragraph(body)))
    
    # Insert tags
    for tag in frontmatter.get('tags', []):
        db.execute('INSERT OR IGNORE INTO tags (entry_id, tag) VALUES (?, ?)', (entry_id, tag))
    
    # Insert builds_on relationships
    for target in frontmatter.get('builds_on', []):
        db.execute('INSERT OR IGNORE INTO relationships (source_id, target_id, rel_type) VALUES (?, ?, ?)',
                   (entry_id, target, 'builds_on'))

# Step 3: Import SOPs (storage/coordination/sops/sop_*.json)
for filepath in sorted(glob.glob('storage/coordination/sops/sop_*.json')):
    data = json.load(open(filepath))
    sop_id = extract_sop_id(filepath)  # e.g., 'SOP-011'
    numeric_id = int(sop_id.split('-')[1])
    
    db.execute('''INSERT INTO entries (id, numeric_id, resource_type, title, summary,
        status, file_path, content_hash, created_date, version, description)
        VALUES (?, ?, 'SOP', ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)''',
        (sop_id, numeric_id, data.get('title', ''), truncate(data.get('description', ''), 200),
         data.get('status', 'active'), filepath,
         hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(data).encode()).hexdigest(),
         data.get('date', ''), data.get('version', '1.0'), data.get('description', '')))
    # Handle supersedes relationships
    if data.get('superseded_by'):
        # Mark relationship when the superseding SOP is also imported
        pass

# Step 4: Import Sources (storage/sources/SRC-*.json)
for filepath in sorted(glob.glob('storage/sources/SRC-*.json')):
    data = json.load(open(filepath))
    src_id = data['id']  # e.g., 'SRC-0001'
    numeric_id = int(src_id.split('-')[1])
    extra = json.dumps({'url': data.get('url'), 'data_types': data.get('data_types', []),
                        'access_type': data.get('access_type', 'unknown')})
    
    db.execute('''INSERT INTO entries (id, numeric_id, resource_type, title, summary,
        file_path, content_hash, extra_json, description)
        VALUES (?, ?, 'SRC', ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)''',
        (src_id, numeric_id, data['name'], truncate(data.get('description', ''), 200),
         filepath, hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(data).encode()).hexdigest(), extra,
         data.get('description', '')))
    
    for tag in data.get('tags', []) + data.get('data_types', []):
        db.execute('INSERT OR IGNORE INTO tags (entry_id, tag) VALUES (?, ?)', (src_id, tag))

# Step 5: Import Scripts (from storage/scripts/index.json)
scripts_index = json.load(open('storage/scripts/index.json'))
for script in scripts_index.get('scripts', []):
    scr_id = script['id']
    numeric_id = int(scr_id.split('-')[1])
    extra = json.dumps({'filename': script.get('filename'), 'language': script.get('language'),
                        'dependencies': script.get('dependencies', [])})
    
    db.execute('''INSERT INTO entries (id, numeric_id, resource_type, title, summary,
        category, file_path, created_date, team, extra_json, description)
        VALUES (?, ?, 'SCR', ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)''',
        (scr_id, numeric_id, script['name'], truncate(script.get('description', ''), 200),
         script.get('category'), 'storage/scripts/' + script.get('filename', ''),
         script.get('added'), script.get('added_by_team'), extra,
         script.get('description', '')))
    
    for tag in script.get('tags', []):
        db.execute('INSERT OR IGNORE INTO tags (entry_id, tag) VALUES (?, ?)', (scr_id, tag))

# Step 6: Import API Tools (from storage/api-tools/index.json)
tools_index = json.load(open('storage/api-tools/index.json'))
for tool in tools_index.get('tools', []):
    tool_id = tool['id']
    numeric_id = int(tool_id.split('-')[1])
    extra = json.dumps({'path': tool.get('path'), 'auth_type': tool.get('auth_type'),
                        'modules': tool.get('modules', []), 'entry_point': tool.get('entry_point'),
                        'requires': tool.get('requires', [])})
    
    db.execute('''INSERT INTO entries (id, numeric_id, resource_type, title, summary,
        category, file_path, created_date, team, extra_json, description)
        VALUES (?, ?, 'TOOL', ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)''',
        (tool_id, numeric_id, tool['name'], truncate(tool.get('description', ''), 200),
         tool.get('category'), 'storage/api-tools/' + tool.get('path', ''),
         tool.get('date_added'), tool.get('team'), extra,
         tool.get('description', '')))
    
    for tag in tool.get('tags', []):
        db.execute('INSERT OR IGNORE INTO tags (entry_id, tag) VALUES (?, ?)', (tool_id, tag))

# Step 7: Import Team Session Logs (teams/sessions/TEAM-*.md)
teams_index = json.load(open('teams/sessions/index.json'))
for session in teams_index.get('sessions', []):
    team_id = session['team_id']
    numeric_id = int(team_id.split('-')[1])
    extra = json.dumps({'filename': session.get('filename'), 'members': session.get('members', [])})
    
    db.execute('''INSERT INTO entries (id, numeric_id, resource_type, title, summary,
        file_path, created_date, team, extra_json, description)
        VALUES (?, ?, 'TEAM', ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)''',
        (team_id, numeric_id, session.get('objective', team_id),
         truncate(session.get('objective', ''), 200),
         'teams/sessions/' + session.get('filename', ''),
         session.get('date'), team_id, extra,
         session.get('objective', '')))
    
    for kb_ref in session.get('builds_on_knowledge', []):
        db.execute('INSERT OR IGNORE INTO relationships (source_id, target_id, rel_type) VALUES (?, ?, ?)',
                   (team_id, kb_ref, 'builds_on'))

# Step 8: Update ID sequences to reflect current max IDs
for rtype in ['KB', 'SOP', 'SRC', 'SCR', 'TEAM', 'TOOL']:
    result = db.execute('SELECT MAX(numeric_id) FROM entries WHERE resource_type = ?', (rtype,)).fetchone()
    max_id = result[0] if result[0] else 0
    db.execute('UPDATE id_sequences SET next_id = ? WHERE resource_type = ?', (max_id + 1, rtype))

# Step 9: Rebuild FTS index (in case of bulk import without triggers)
db.execute("INSERT INTO entries_fts(entries_fts) VALUES ('rebuild');")

db.commit()
db.close()

# Step 10: Generate static files for zero-dependency access
# SUMMARY.json (Level 0, ~50 tokens)
summary_data = db.execute('SELECT * FROM v_summary').fetchall()
write_json('SUMMARY.json', format_summary(summary_data))

# INDEX_COMPACT.json (Level 1, ~500 tokens)
compact_data = db.execute('SELECT * FROM v_compact').fetchall()
write_json('INDEX_COMPACT.json', format_compact(compact_data))
